purpose: Defines the multidimensional spatial model used by the interactive belief atlas.
principle: The cube is a visualization, not a claim that political or religious life can be reduced to three numbers. The underlying lexicons remain richer and each coordinate is an analytical approximation.

political.name: Political Cube
political.quadrants: Every horizontal slice is the familiar four-quadrant compass: economic left/right × authority libertarian/authoritarian. The third dimension changes the slice rather than replacing the classic compass.

religious.name: Religious Worldview Cube
religious.principle: Religious traditions are not assigned political left/right coordinates. Their cube uses dimensions appropriate to religious-worldview comparison instead.

projection.camera: drag to rotate; wheel to zoom
projection.selection: hover previews a record; click opens belief.html?id=<slug>
projection.slices: the classic 2D compass is a horizontal slice through the political cube

coordinate_policy.source: Existing political lexicon coordinates are retained as economic and authority scores. Social-openness values are derived deterministically from the existing label/definition until each record receives an explicitly researched third-axis score. Religious coordinates are visual indexes rather than claims about truth or political affiliation.
